key_insight: A digital twin can evaluate local collective tariffs by simulating household behavior, shared metering, and tariff rules together, revealing how aggregation changes community costs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical engineering framework for testing tariff designs under realistic demand, PV, battery, and EV charging conditions before deployment.
method: Agent-based simulation of household consumption and local generation
Virtual aggregation via shared metering within one digital twin environment
Embedded tariff logic to compare community-level cost outcomes
evidence_signal: The method was demonstrated on the Danish Local Collective Tariff across representative residential community scenarios with PV, battery storage, and EV charging, showing measurable cost reductions from aggregation.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on the timing match between consumption and generation, so fairness and cost neutrality may vary across participants.
paper_title: A Digital Twin-Based Method for Evaluating Local Collective Tariffs in Distribution-Level Energy Systems
